newNodes.description: Compute reliability over a mission time from a constant failure rate, and relate failure rate, MTBF and probability of surviving a given duration.

newNodes.name: Reliability of series and redundant systems
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Calculate system reliability from component reliabilities for series chains and parallel redundancy, and identify the weakest elements.

newNodes.name: Failure modes and effects analysis
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Perform a failure modes and effects analysis listing each component failure mode, its effects, causes and detection, and rank them by severity, occurrence and detection.

newNodes.name: Build and evaluate a fault tree
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Build a fault tree for an undesired top event such as an uncommanded arm motion and compute its probability from basic event probabilities.

newNodes.name: Plan burn-in to remove early failures
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Use the bathtub curve to plan a burn-in period for new actuators and electronics that exposes early-life failures before the robot is used with people.

newNodes.name: Confidence bounds on task success rate
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Compute a confidence interval for a task success rate from repeated trials and determine how many trials are needed to claim a target rate.

newNodes.name: Run repeat-run endurance tests
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Run a task many times under controlled conditions, record every outcome and failure, and report success rate with confidence bounds and failure modes.

newNodes.name: Track cycle counts and component wear
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Track joint cycles, cable flexes, operating hours and measured backlash per component to predict wear-out and schedule replacement.

newNodes.name: Write a preventive maintenance plan
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Write a preventive maintenance schedule of inspections, lubrication, recalibration and replacements derived from wear data and the FMEA.

newNodes.name: Plan spares and swappable modules
newNodes.subject: Reliability and maintenance
newNodes.description: Choose which modules to stock as spares from failure likelihood, repair time and lead time, and design for quick module swaps.

newNodes.name: Identify robot hazards systematically
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Identify mechanical, electrical, thermal, behavioral and environmental hazards across every use case and lifecycle phase from assembly to disposal.

newNodes.name: Estimate risk with a severity-probability matrix
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Rate each hazard's severity and likelihood on defined scales, place it on a risk matrix, and decide whether the risk is acceptable.

newNodes.name: Apply the risk reduction hierarchy
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Reduce risk in priority order: inherently safe design, then safeguards and protective devices, then warnings and training, and justify each choice.

newNodes.name: Specify robot safety functions
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Specify safety functions such as protective stop, speed limiting, zone limiting and torque limiting, each with trigger, response, response time and safe state.

newNodes.name: Stop categories and safe torque off
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Distinguish stop categories 0, 1 and 2 and safe torque off, and select which applies to each joint given gravity loads and brakes.

newNodes.name: Define safe states for each failure
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Define what each subsystem does on fault, power loss or communication loss, such as braking, holding or going limp, and check the result is actually safe.

newNodes.name: Review an emergency stop design
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Review an emergency stop circuit for independence from software, single-fault behavior, reset logic, reachability and periodic testing.

newNodes.name: Identify and mitigate pinch and crush points
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Find pinch, crush and shear points in arms, hands, neck and torso joints and mitigate them with gaps, covers, torque limits or geometry changes.

newNodes.name: Assess tip-over hazard of a tall mobile robot
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Compute tip-over margins of a tall wheeled humanoid during acceleration, braking, slopes and arm extension, and set motion limits to keep it stable.

newNodes.name: Plan lithium battery fire safety
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Plan safe charging, storage, transport and damaged-cell handling for lithium packs, and define the response to swelling, smoke or thermal runaway.

newNodes.name: Review electrical safety of a robot
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Review fusing, wire ratings, insulation, strain relief, touch-accessible voltages and grounding against the wiring diagram, and record nonconformities.

newNodes.name: Navigate type A, B and C safety standards
newNodes.subject: Safety standards awareness
newNodes.description: Explain how basic, group and product safety standards relate and locate which ones apply to a service humanoid robot.

newNodes.name: ISO 12100 risk assessment process
newNodes.subject: Safety standards awareness
newNodes.description: Apply the ISO 12100 sequence of determining limits, identifying hazards, estimating and evaluating risk, and reducing it iteratively, for a robot.

newNodes.name: ISO 10218 industrial robot safety concepts
newNodes.subject: Safety standards awareness
newNodes.description: Explain ISO 10218 concepts such as protective stops, reduced speed, enabling devices and safeguarded spaces, and which transfer to a service robot.

newNodes.name: ISO/TS 15066 collaborative operation
newNodes.subject: Safety standards awareness
newNodes.description: Explain the four collaborative operation modes and body-region contact limits of ISO/TS 15066, and when each mode suits a human-facing robot.

newNodes.name: ISO 13482 personal care robot concepts
newNodes.subject: Safety standards awareness
newNodes.description: Explain how ISO 13482 classifies personal care robots and the hazards it emphasizes, such as instability, contact and autonomous behavior errors.

newNodes.name: Functional safety: IEC 61508 SIL and ISO 13849 PL
newNodes.subject: Safety standards awareness
newNodes.description: Explain safety integrity levels and performance levels, how architecture, diagnostics and failure rates determine them, and why software alone rarely suffices.

newNodes.name: Speed and separation monitoring
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Compute the protective separation distance from human speed, robot speed, reaction time and stopping distance, and set speed limits for detected people.

newNodes.name: Power and force limiting
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Estimate contact force and transferred energy from effective mass and speed, and set joint speed and torque limits to stay below body-region thresholds.

newNodes.name: Measure collision forces on a robot
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Measure peak and quasi-static contact forces with a force gauge or instrumented target and compare them with allowed limits for each body region.

newNodes.name: Bound autonomous behavior with a safety supervisor
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Design a supervisor, independent of AI planners, that enforces speed, force, zone and mode limits on every commanded action and can veto unsafe commands.

newNodes.name: Robot risk assessment
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Produce a full risk assessment for a human-facing robot listing hazards, risk estimates, chosen measures and residual risk, following the ISO 12100 process.

newNodes.name: Validate safety functions by test
newNodes.subject: Safety engineering
newNodes.description: Verify each safety function by test, such as measuring e-stop stopping time and distance and confirming safe states under injected faults, and record evidence.

newNodes.name: Threat-model a networked robot
newNodes.subject: Cybersecurity
newNodes.description: Identify assets, entry points and attackers for a networked robot and enumerate threats such as spoofed commands, data theft and denial of service.

newNodes.name: Harden robot network services
newNodes.subject: Cybersecurity
newNodes.description: Close unused ports, use key-based SSH, change default credentials, enable a firewall and restrict middleware discovery to trusted hosts.

newNodes.name: Deploy signed updates with rollback
newNodes.subject: Cybersecurity
newNodes.description: Deploy software and firmware updates that are authenticated, staged and reversible, so a failed or tampered update cannot leave the robot unsafe.

newNodes.name: Secure remote command and teleoperation
newNodes.subject: Cybersecurity
newNodes.description: Authenticate remote operators, authorize which commands they may send, and make the robot stop safely when the remote link drops or lags.

newNodes.name: Review privacy of cameras and microphones
newNodes.subject: Ethics and privacy
newNodes.description: Assess what audio, video and personal data the droid captures, stores and sends, and apply minimization, retention limits, local processing and consent.

newNodes.name: Review ethics of a humanlike social robot
newNodes.subject: Ethics and privacy
newNodes.description: Review risks of deception, overtrust, emotional dependence, vulnerable users and unclear AI disclosure, and decide design measures for each.

newNodes.name: Build a work breakdown structure
newNodes.subject: Project management
newNodes.description: Decompose the robot project into deliverable-oriented work packages that cover all hardware, software, testing and documentation work.

newNodes.name: Define milestones with entry and exit criteria
newNodes.subject: Project management
newNodes.description: Define project milestones with clear demonstrable exit criteria tied to requirements and tests, rather than effort spent.

newNodes.name: Build a schedule and find the critical path
newNodes.subject: Project management
newNodes.description: Build a dependency-based schedule with durations and lead times, compute the critical path and slack, and identify which delays move the end date.

newNodes.name: Track actual versus planned cost
newNodes.subject: Project management
newNodes.description: Track actual spending against the cost budget by work package, forecast the cost at completion, and flag overruns early.

newNodes.name: Maintain a project risk register
newNodes.subject: Project management
newNodes.description: Keep a register of technical, schedule and supply risks with likelihood, impact, owner, mitigation and trigger, and review it at each milestone.

newNodes.name: Control scope and descope deliberately
newNodes.subject: Project management
newNodes.description: Evaluate proposed feature additions against schedule and budget, define a minimum viable demonstration, and descope features with documented reasoning.

newNodes.name: Review a design for manufacture and assembly
newNodes.subject: Design for manufacture and cost
newNodes.description: Review parts and assemblies for part count, process suitability, fastener commonality, tolerance needs and assembly access, and propose simplifications.

newNodes.name: Reduce cost through value engineering
newNodes.subject: Design for manufacture and cost
newNodes.description: Find cost drivers in the bill of materials, compare should-cost estimates with quotes, and redesign or resource parts without breaking requirements.

newNodes.name: Design for serviceability
newNodes.subject: Design for manufacture and cost
newNodes.description: Arrange modules, connectors and fasteners so common repairs and replacements are fast, safe and need few tools, and measure swap time.

newNodes.name: Plan a field trial
newNodes.subject: Field trials and acceptance
newNodes.description: Plan a trial in a real setting with protocol, metrics, observers, safety supervision, participant briefing, stop rules and data handling.

newNodes.name: Measure usability and user satisfaction
newNodes.subject: Field trials and acceptance
newNodes.description: Measure task success, completion time, interventions and questionnaire scores such as SUS, and summarize them with appropriate statistics.

newNodes.name: Report incidents and near misses
newNodes.subject: Field trials and acceptance
newNodes.description: Record incidents and near misses during trials with conditions, logs and immediate actions, and feed them back into the risk assessment.

newNodes.name: Run user acceptance testing
newNodes.subject: Field trials and acceptance
newNodes.description: Run acceptance tests with intended users against criteria traced to stakeholder needs and decide whether the robot is accepted, conditionally accepted or rejected.

newNodes.name: Integrate two arms on a torso
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Mount two arms on a torso with shared power and communication, a common base frame, mass checks and inter-arm collision limits, and verify each arm in place.

newNodes.name: Integrate hands at the wrists
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Integrate hands onto both arms, routing cables or tendons through the wrists, defining the wrist interface, and verifying grasp function after mounting.

newNodes.name: Integrate head and neck with cameras and microphones
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Integrate an actuated neck and sensor head, calibrate cameras and microphones to the torso frame, and verify gaze pointing accuracy.

newNodes.name: Integrate the expressive face into the head
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Integrate a face display or actuated features into the head, checking brightness, viewing angle, heat, cable routing and synchronization with speech.

newNodes.name: Integrate the speech pipeline on the robot
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Run microphones, speech recognition, dialogue and speech synthesis on the robot, handling motor self-noise, echo, barge-in and the end-to-end latency budget.

newNodes.name: Bring up coordinated upper-body control
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Bring up coordinated control of torso, both arms and neck with self-collision avoidance and joint limits, and verify combined motions at reduced speed.

newNodes.name: Mount the upper body on the wheeled base
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Mount the humanoid upper body on a wheeled base, merge power and networks, update stability limits, and verify driving with the upper body powered.

newNodes.name: Verify full-system power and runtime
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Power the complete humanoid through its distribution system, measure current under representative tasks, and verify runtime, brownout behavior and battery limits.

newNodes.name: Integrate a task executive with language commands
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Connect dialogue and LLM tool calls to robot skills through a task executive that checks mode, preconditions and safety limits before each action.

newNodes.name: Integrate legs in place of the wheeled base
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Replace the wheeled base with a leg module, update the hip interface, mass properties and models, and test on a gantry with fall protection.

newNodes.name: Manage falls of a bipedal humanoid
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration
newNodes.description: Plan fall protection with gantries and tethers, detect imminent falls, command a protective falling posture and inspect for damage after any fall.

newNodes.name: Milestone I06: integrate and verify a humanoid upper body
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration milestones
newNodes.description: Integrate torso, two arms with hands and an expressive head, then verify coordinated bimanual and head motion against requirements with test reports and an updated FMEA.

newNodes.name: Milestone I07: integrate a wheeled humanoid that navigates and manipulates
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration milestones
newNodes.description: Integrate the upper body on a wheeled base that navigates among people and performs pick-and-place tasks, verified by repeat-run tests within power and stability limits.

newNodes.name: Milestone I08: verify a conversational protocol droid that performs tasks safely
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration milestones
newNodes.description: Verify a droid that converses, takes spoken requests, performs tasks through guarded tool calls and passes risk assessment, safety validation, privacy review and user acceptance.

newNodes.name: Milestone I09 (optional): integrate bipedal locomotion into the humanoid
newNodes.subject: Humanoid integration milestones
newNodes.description: Integrate legs into the verified protocol droid so it walks on a physical biped platform, with fall safety, updated risk assessment and repeat-run walking trials.
